I think we're already starting to reach that tipping point for this sort of software. The current upvote system just doesn't work so well when conversations get big because the vast majority of posts end up receiving close to 0 exposure regardless of their quality and those that do receive exposure are not necessarily the most interesting comments. For instance a relatively mediocre comment that gets upvoted early on will end up getting more exposure and more upvotes and thus end up at the top while more interesting comment that didn't receive that early upvote receive less visibility and thus never reach that 'critical mass' required to receive visibility. And interesting comments that are buried in a reply chain will never end up getting seen at all by most people.

I'd like to see Voat grow, but I think there needs to be some major improvement to the style or presentation of comments. There are a lot of possible ideas. Just off the top of my head:

  • Start featuring wildcard comments in prominent locations a topic. These comments are randomly chosen each time a page is viewed and do little more than put more eyeballs on comments that otherwise would never be seen, giving them a chance to grab some upvotes if deserving and filter on up through the comments.

  • Break conversation into buckets. Instead of having thousands of people all try to discuss something in one incoherent mess, instead break it down into large numbers of groups of, for instance, 100. People could freely change to another bucket by clicking a button, but once they comment or vote in one bucket all their comments/votes are constrained to being in that bucket (although you can read any other bucket). And if there are already too many people commenting in a certain bucket then new posters would be forced to find a different bucket to avoid creating 'mega buckets'. Incidentally this would also have a nice effect on cutting out shilling and vote manipulation. It'd also be interesting to see how different independent buckets come to different conclusions depending on the comments made, or if most buckets end up coming to the same conclusion. The idea is to allow the pleasant conversation that this software allows with relatively few numbers of users while not constraining it against growth of the site.

I don't mind the site becoming huge if we have quality content and discussion. What I really don't want is the avalanche of pun threads, circle jerks and other insider joke one-liners that pollute the other site these days.
